issues.issue: The preamble licenses to "you" and to "the ARP POV System, described above," both of which are fixed only by the web-form page above, which names Garrett Salpeter individually while listing his employer as ARPwave Austin LLC and describes no system beyond "Quantity of Plans: 4." Who the "Licensee" is and what property is licensed are therefore open on the face of the instrument.

"[U]nder no conditions can the POV be used commercially" leaves "commercially" undefined — whether it bars only resale or also use on paying clients in the Licensee's own practice is not fixed anywhere in the agreement.

The declaration that the agreement "is non-cancellable for any reason and under no conditions" cannot be squared with Section 7.1, which presumes termination "upon [Licensee's] default," and Section 7.2, which speaks of "termination of this Agreement for any reason." Whether the instrument can be terminated at all is left to be construed.

Section 1.2 says the licensed ARP POV SYSTEM "consists of" five enumerated items, while Section 1.1 defines System(s) as all protocols, programs, intellectual property and equipment "associated with ARP Wave LLC." The enumerated list and the open-ended definition give the same defined term two different extensions.

The term is keyed to a "License Start Date" and "License End Date" "set forth on page one of this Agreement," and to post-term "rates set forth on page one," but page one is an order form containing no such dates and no such rate schedule. The commencement, expiry and post-term charges are left without a referent.

The rights are said to be "forfeitable in the event of certain circumstances or occurrences as herein set forth," but no forfeiture circumstances are set out anywhere in this agreement, unlike the automatic-revocation list in the 2010 License Agreement. The triggering events for forfeiture are undefined.

Section 1.5 forbids Licensee to "make enhancements or modify, or alter the System(s)" without written consent, yet Section 7.2 requires return on termination of "all originals, copies or renditions or enhancements" of the System(s), and this agreement omits the 2010 agreement's clause vesting enhancements in Licensor. Ownership of any enhancement that is in fact made is left unresolved between the two sections.

Repairs are free unless "the required repair is determined to be the result of misuse or negligence," and the passive phrasing does not say who makes that determination or by what standard. The clause also limits free repair to "the original term" while Section 1.3 lets the unit stay with Licensee indefinitely afterwards.

The insurance floor is "the full replacement value thereof as determined by the Licensor; which presently is $7560.00" — a figure that neither matches the $7500 total price on page one nor states whether Licensor may unilaterally revise it. Whether the fixed sum or Licensor's later determination controls is left open.

"[A]cting outside the scope of use for the System(s)" and "the Protocols licensed in conjunction with the System(s)" are neither defined nor identified, and "Protocols" appears nowhere as a defined term. The content of the compliance duty is therefore unfixed.

Section 3.2 bars Licensee from making the System(s) "available to any other party" without written consent, while Section 3.1 and Section 7.4 presuppose application of the unit by an "applicator" to an "applicatee." Whether ordinary use on another person is a prohibited disclosure has to be construed between the two.

The disclaimer excludes "warranties of marketability" rather than warranties of merchantability, a word substitution that on its face fails to name the implied warranty it is meant to negate. Whether the merchantability warranty is disclaimed turns on that error.

The first sentence preserves claims "for any breach or breaches of Licensor's contractual obligations herein set forth," while the second waives "any consequences, damages or any form of redress with respect to said System(s)." The two sentences of the same paragraph cannot both be given full effect.

The no-results disclaimer runs only to results "Licensee will achieve," dropping the 2010 agreement's reference to "Licensee's clients" and saying nothing about the "applicatee" contemplated by Section 3.1. Its reach as to third parties treated with the unit is unstated.

Section 5.1 begins "Notwithstanding any said repossession" and waives damages "upon the occurrence of an event of default under this section," yet Section 5 contains no definition of default and no repossession remedy at all, unlike the enumerated remedy lists in the 2010 Lease and License Agreements. The provision's operative references point to text that is not in the instrument.

The clause indemnifies enforcement costs under "this License Agreement or any related agreements" but cross-defaults only agreements "signed contemporaneously" between the parties; neither "related" nor "contemporaneously" is defined, and the 2010 agreements were signed years earlier. The set of agreements caught by the cross-default is unfixed.

By making a default under "any other agreement signed contemporaneously between Licensor and Licensee" a default here, Section 5.2 presupposes other operative agreements, which cannot be squared with Section 7.7's statement that "[t]his License constitutes the entire agreement between the parties hereto." Whether the earlier ARP Wave agreements remain in force alongside this one turns on reading the two together.

The notice clause supplies an address only "TO LICENSOR" and leaves the Licensee notice block missing entirely, so no address exists at which Licensee may be served under the agreement. The Licensor address given (Apple Valley, MN 55337) also differs from the 55124 zip in the preamble.

The middle of Section 7.1 is unintelligible on the face of the document — the text between "terminated upon" and "any rights herein set forth shall be deemed to be automatically revoked" is garbled beyond reading. What termination events trigger automatic revocation and reassignment cannot be determined from the words.

Section 7.2 requires immediate return of all System(s) "[u]pon termination of this Agreement for any reason," which cannot be squared with Section 1.3, permitting the System(s) to "remain in the possession of the Licensee" at no charge once the original term ends, or with Section 1.1's "non-cancellable" declaration. When the return duty is triggered has to be construed across those provisions.

The clause binds Licensee to "the instructions contained in the ARP Unit Manual" and its "Cautionary and Warning language," a document that is neither defined, attached, nor identified by date or version. The content of the obligation depends wholly on an extrinsic writing.

Section 7.6 permits Licensor to assign "without notice to the Licensee," while Section 7.8 separately governs Licensor assignment as being "without the prior written consent of Licensee," and neither says whether Licensor's obligations survive an assignment. Which of the two overlapping assignment clauses states the operative condition is left to construction.

The integration clause declares this License "the entire agreement between the parties," but Section 5.2 cross-defaults "any related agreements" and "any other agreement signed contemporaneously," and Section 7.9 extends the forum clause to "ANY RELATED AGREEMENTS." Whether the earlier ARP Wave lease and license agreements were superseded cannot be answered from Section 7.7 alone.

Section 7.8's bar on assignment or sublicense by Licensee duplicates Section 1.4, which also declares any attempted transfer "a material breach," while 7.8 attaches no stated consequence, and its Licensor-assignment sentence overlaps Section 7.6. The consequence of a Licensee transfer and the conditions of a Licensor assignment must be pieced together from the several clauses.

The clause compels litigation in Hennepin County of "ALL ACTIONS OR PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT OR ANY RELATED AGREEMENTS," and "related agreements" is nowhere defined or bounded. Whether it captures the separate 2010 individual agreements and the clinic lease and license, and non-contract claims, is open on the text.

The extension of the forum clause to "ANY RELATED AGREEMENTS" presupposes other subsisting agreements, which sits against Section 7.7's declaration that this License is the entire agreement between the parties. Which provision controls determines whether disputes under the earlier agreements are swept into Minnesota.

The blue-pencil sentence directs that a provision "so broad as to be unenforceable" "shall be sufficiently narrowed so as to make it enforceable," without saying who narrows it or by what standard. Applied to the sweeping waivers in Sections 4.2 and 5.1, the degree of narrowing is undetermined.
